title: Self-dual / anti-self-dual split of the Weyl tensor in oriented Riemannian 4-space
expression_sketch: Oriented Riemannian 4-manifold (or algebraic model: oriented Euclidean R^4 with metric g=delta, volume form epsilon, epsilon(1,2,3,4)=+1). Indices a,b,c,d,e,f in {1,2,3,4}. Hodge star on 2-forms: (*omega)(a,b) = (1/2)*Sum_{c,d} epsilon(a,b,c,d)*omega(c,d), equivalently (*omega)_{ab} = (1/2) epsilon_{ab}^{cd} omega_{cd}. Euclidean identity *^2 = +Id on wedge^2. Orthogonal projectors on 2-forms: P_plus(a,b;c,d) = (1/4)*(g(a,c)*g(b,d)-g(a,d)*g(b,c)) + (1/4)*epsilon(a,b,c,d); P_minus(a,b;c,d) = (1/4)*(g(a,c)*g(b,d)-g(a,d)*g(b,c)) - (1/4)*epsilon(a,b,c,d). Algebra: P_plus+P_minus = P_wedge2, P_plus*P_minus=0, P_plus**2=P_plus, P_minus**2=P_minus, Tr P_plus = Tr P_minus = 3 so wedge^2 R^4 = 3 + 3. On a Weyl tensor C (algebraic curvature, totally traceless): left dual (*C)(a,b,c,d) = (1/2)*Sum_{e,f} epsilon(a,b,e,f)*C(e,f,c,d). Self-dual and anti-self-dual pieces: C_plus = (1/2)*(C + *C), C_minus = (1/2)*(C - *C). Reconstruction: C = C_plus + C_minus. Double-dual identity for Weyl in 4D Riemannian signature: *C* = C, equivalently *C_plus = C_plus and *C_minus = -C_minus. Each of C_plus, C_minus is a 5-dimensional SO(4) irrep (the (3,1) and (1,3) of Spin(4)=SU(2)xSU(2)); 5+5=10 independent Weyl components.
latent_structure: Further SO(4) (equivalently SU(2)xSU(2)) irrep split of the 10-dimensional Weyl space beyond the O(n) Ricci--Weyl decomposition. The Hodge star on 2-forms is the extra 4D generator; P_plus/P_minus reconstruct C as a sum of two 5-dimensional chiral pieces. Not the S+E+W split (that uses the metric traces, not epsilon), and not 3D Levi-Civita products.

function_domains.g: Positive-definite Euclidean metric on an oriented 4-dimensional vector space (Kronecker in an orthonormal frame).
function_domains.epsilon: Levi-Civita volume form of that orientation, epsilon(1,2,3,4)=+1, totally antisymmetric on {1,2,3,4}.
function_domains.C: Algebraic Weyl tensor: Riemann symmetries plus total tracelessness g^{ac} C_{abcd}=0.

nonzero_conditions.statement: n=4, so Hodge star maps 2-forms to 2-forms (middle degree). The coefficient 1/2 is defined in Q.
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Wikipedia Weyl tensor: in dimension 4 the Weyl tensor further decomposes into self-dual and anti-self-dual parts C+ and C-; Singer--Thorpe 1969

nonzero_conditions.statement: g is positive definite (Riemannian), so *^2 = +Id on 2-forms and P_plus, P_minus are real.
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Hodge star on an oriented Riemannian 4-manifold; Wikipedia Hodge star, Euclidean middle-degree identity *^2 = 1

positivity_conditions.statement: g is positive definite. (Lorentzian *^2 = -1 on 2-forms would complexify the eigenspaces; that signature is not used.)
positivity_conditions.label: DECLARED
positivity_conditions.source: Wikipedia Hodge star operator, signature dependence of *^2 on 2-forms

branch_conventions: No square roots: epsilon is the algebraic volume tensor of an oriented orthonormal frame, epsilon_1234=+1.
source_provenance: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weyl_tensor (dimension-4 sentence: Weyl further decomposes into self-dual and anti-self-dual parts C+ and C- under SO(4)).
I. M. Singer and J. A. Thorpe, The curvature of 4-dimensional Einstein spaces, Global Analysis (Papers in Honor of K. Kodaira), Univ. Tokyo Press, 1969, pp. 355-365.
M. F. Atiyah, N. J. Hitchin, I. M. Singer, Self-duality in four-dimensional Riemannian geometry, Proc. Roy. Soc. A 362 (1978) 425-461.
A. L. Besse, Einstein Manifolds, Ergebnisse 10, Springer 1987, Ch. 1 (4D Hodge split of Weyl).

derived_conditions.statement: On 2-forms in oriented Euclidean 4-space, * is a linear involution, so the projectors (1/2)(I +- *) are complementary idempotents.
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED

derived_conditions.statement: Weyl's double dual equals itself in 4D Riemannian signature (*C* = C), so the left dual already diagonalizes the chiral split; this uses tracelessness of C (Ricci pieces mix duals via Ruse--Lanczos).
derived_conditions.label: DECLARED
derived_conditions.source: Singer--Thorpe 1969; Besse 1987; Ruse--Lanczos identity reduces to *C = +- C on the Weyl piece

derived_conditions.statement: dim of self-dual Weyl is 5: dim of self-dual 2-forms is 3, and traceless endomorphisms of that 3-space that additionally satisfy the curvature pair-symmetry give a 5-dimensional space (symmetric traceless 3x3).
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: Besse Einstein Manifolds, 4D Weyl discussion; Wikipedia Petrov classification dimension count 10=5+5

public_source: Wikipedia Weyl tensor 4D C+/C- split; Singer--Thorpe 1969; Atiyah--Hitchin--Singer 1978; Besse 1987
why_not_cse_lgg: An expanded 20-component algebraic curvature with traces removed still does not CSE into two chiral 5-blocks. LGG cannot invent the Hodge star as an SO(4) generator. Distinct from the metric Kulkarni--Nomizu Ricci--Weyl split, which exists in every dimension n>=4 and does not use epsilon.
proposer_leak_risk: Hide self-dual, anti-self-dual, Hodge, chiral, Petrov, instanton, C+, C-. Do not print the (I+*)/2 template in proposer context.
notes: Pointwise algebraic identity on an oriented Euclidean 4-dimensional vector space. Riemannian signature is declared so that *^2=+1 and the projectors are real. Distinct from ac-t-ricci-weyl (S+E+W, no Hodge) and ac-t-eps-delta (3D Levi-Civita products).
